Titan Equipment Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Titan Equipment Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Titan Equipment Inc.'s results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Titan Equipment Inc.'s performance for the second quarter of 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We saw strong order intake and book-to-bill trends across end markets like construction, mining, and agriculture. Lead times for our key products and components continued to improve meaningfully. Inventory levels are well-managed with effective strategies in place. Revenue grew solidly across geographic regions. Organic revenue growth was robust, complemented by contributions from recent acquisitions. Macroeconomic factors influenced end market demand in a balanced way. Our automation and digital offerings accelerated, boosting efficiency. Demand trends in construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing remained resilient overall.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

David Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Michael. Turning to our financial performance, Titan Equipment Inc. reported $2.75 billion in revenue for the second quarter, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 42%, driven by favorable product mix, pricing discipline, and operational efficiencies. Operating expenses were $680 million, resulting in an operating income of $490 million. Our net income for the quarter was $360 million, or $2.25 per share.

Let me expand on these results by diving into the key aspects underscoring our performance. First, on order intake and book-to-bill trends by end market. Total order intake reached $2.8 billion in Q2, up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially from Q1. This marks our strongest quarterly bookings since Q4 2022, driven by robust demand in infrastructure-related end markets and selective wins in resource sectors. Our trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio stands at a healthy 1.22x, with backlog visibility extending to 14 months at current production rates—up from 12 months a year ago. This positions us well for sustained revenue growth into FY25, even as we navigate softening commodity cycles.

Breaking it down by key end markets—construction, mining, and agriculture, which collectively represent 72% of our order intake—construction remains our growth engine, with orders surging 22% year-over-year to $1.15 billion, led by demand for mid-tonnage excavators like our HX300 series with 35-ton capacity and hybrid powertrains, and rigid-frame wheel loaders similar to Caterpillar's 988K. Sequentially, intake rose 12%, reflecting capex recovery. Book-to-bill here printed at 1.35x for the quarter—our highest in three years—pushing segment backlog to $4.2 billion, up 25% YoY, with 16-month visibility supported by multi-year contracts. Regionally, North America drove 55% of segment intake with 35% YoY growth fueled by the IIJA's $1.2 trillion tailwinds and state-level programs, including a $250 million fleet deal for autonomous-ready dozers with Trimble-like GPS and telematics. EMEA added 25% with 15% growth in Germany and the Nordics on EU Green Deal rail and urban renewal, where our electrified mini-excavators like the 10-ton eHX model captured 12% market share gains versus Volvo CE. Asia-Pacific and LatAm were mixed at 20%, with India's infrastructure boom offsetting China real estate weakness. We're leaning into digital twins and AI-optimized site planning via TitanConnect, boosting order conversion by 18% for connected machines, positioning us ahead of peers like Komatsu in Tier 4 Final emissions-compliant fleets.

In mining, orders totaled $504 million, up 12% YoY but flat sequentially as customers digest prior capex. Demand focused on ultra-class haul trucks like our MT785 with 400-ton payload and e-drive akin to Liebherr's T 264, and high-capacity shovels amid steady copper and gold exposure despite iron ore volatility. Book-to-bill was 1.15x, backlog $1.8 billion up 10% YoY with 13-month visibility, reflecting 8% higher average selling prices on premium autonomy packages and aftermarket pull-through. APAC/Australia led at 45% with 20% growth from Pilbara expansions and Indonesian nickel projects, securing a $180 million order for 15 MT785 trucks with BEV retrofits aligning with Rio Tinto decarbonization. North America 30% at +8%, with Nevada gold and Permian potash; LatAm/Africa 25% at +5%, steady Peruvian copper but South African platinum delays. Modular Mining Acquisition integration rolled out autonomous haulage to 20 sites, improving cycle times 15% and driving 25% of Q2 orders, targeting 20% market share by 2026 ahead of Sandvik and Epiroc.

Agriculture faced headwinds from 15% lower YoY grain prices and farmer caution, with orders at $364 million—down 4% YoY but +3% sequentially on early planting. Strength in precision ag tractors like AGPro 500 series 500HP with John Deere-like AutoTrac offset combine weakness. Book-to-bill 0.92x, backlog steady at $850 million with 10-month visibility, protecting margins via OEM upgrades. North America 60% flat; EMEA 20% -2% with EU subsidies for sprayers but drought pressure; Asia/LatAm 20% -10% with Indian tractor pullback. Launching biomass-compatible harvesters and AI-yield optimization via TitanFarm IoT captured 10% sustainable ag share, with CNH partnerships expanding 30-50HP, Q3 inflecting on harvest.

Other segments: energy & power 15% +25% to $420M with gas turbine and wind OEM, book-to-bill 1.4x; industrial 13% flat on factory automation. Overall 1.22x book-to-bill with 65% Q3 revenue booked, margins from 22% high-spec mix and 28% services. Risks China slowdown, ag destocking offset by +2pts share to 14% global and $500M FY24 tech capex. Q3 intake $2.6-2.9B, FY24 book-to-bill 1.15-1.25x.

Next, lead times for key products and components. Underpinning our $4.2 billion backlog up 18% YoY, we've compressed lead times amid raw material inflation and labor shortages, enhancing our edge versus Caterpillar and Siemens. Flagship precision CNC machining centers—MX-500 series, 35% mix for automotive/aerospace like Ford/Boeing—dropped to 14 weeks from 22, 36% improvement via Dayton Phase II expansion adding 25% spindle hours with automated pallet changers and AI toolpathing from Autodesk. Heavy-duty hydraulic presses for EV battery stamping now 18 weeks from 28, via steel alloy stockpiling despite Red Sea issues.

Components: electronic control modules like Siemens PLCs with IoT edge for predictive maintenance improved 42% to 7 weeks from 12, via multi-sourcing to Mexico/Vietnam reducing Asian exposure 60% and TSMC alternatives for SiC inverters. Castings/forgings at 10 weeks for gray iron, 25% reduction, via new Monterrey induction furnace de-risking from ArcelorMittal, halving transit.

Regionally: North America 55% bookings at 15 weeks best-in-class vs ISM 20+, CHIPS/IRA aiding semi fab with Texas/Michigan hubs. EMEA 20 weeks challenged by energy/Ukraine, Düsseldorf warehouse shaving 3 weeks for wind gear reducers. APAC 16 weeks, Taiwan partnerships offset Typhoon Yagi via Singapore stocking.

'ForgeForward' $250M program uses Siemens NX digital twins for 92% forecast accuracy up from 78%, RFID kanban reducing WIP 22% JIT like Toyota. Q3 another 10-15% compression with Gen4 additive for titanium aero. Gains convert 12% more quotes, capturing $450B market as capex rebounds.

On inventory levels and management strategies, total inventory $1.28 billion, +3% QoQ from $1.24B but -8% YoY from $1.39B peak. DSI 72 days vs S&P 82, turns 5.1x up from 4.6x, freeing $110M working capital. Normalization post-2022 95-day balloon from semis/steel; unwound 75% as steel -15% YoY PPI, WIP 42% from 48%.

North America $700M 55%, DSI 65 days reshoring CHIPS/IRA for semi/EV, no stockouts AI data centers. EMEA $320M +5% QoQ energy crisis, wind softening rare earth safety stock DSI 85. APAC $260M flat, -20% China forgings to Vietnam/India.

Strategies: SAP S/4HANA-Palantir AI ERP 92% forecast accuracy on 15yr data/BOM 5000+ SKUs. 75% JIT/VMI with Timken/Bosch Rexroth cutting owned $85M, IoT RFID 90% pallets dashboard cycle -18% pilferage <0.2%. Digital twins Siemens NX stress-test buffers, safety stock 12% adjustable -3pts service 98.5%. Protected 28.4% gross amid +7% aluminum, CCC 55 from 68 days funding $250M buybacks/R&D. Q4 DSI 68-70 ramp US infra/EU green, hedged strikes/Ukraine with multi-source/$200M forwards.

Revenue performance by geographic region: consolidated $2.48B +9% YoY +11% CC, 8th organic quarter, backlog $5.2B +15%, core +10% post-divestiture. Tailwinds reshoring, Industry 4.0, electrification. Americas 45% $1.12B +14%/+16% CC, outpacing Cat/Deere, PrecisionCNC lathes/mills +22% CHIPS/IRA Midwest/Southeast PMI>50, EquipGuard IoT 65% adoption ASP +7%, 80% NA content, $150M Fort Wayne robotics capex 20% cobot share FY25.

EMEA 28% $694M +4%/+7% CC euro headwinds, Europe 85% Germany/Nordics +9% AutoPalletizer BEV retool VW/Stellantis, UK/South -3% energy/capex, ME +18% Aramco pumps, Africa mining. Digital twin Siemens MindSphere 15% bookings, ECB cuts, 70% euro hedge, sustainability for Green Deal actuators.

APAC 24% $595M +6%/+9% CC India/SE offset China -5% property/tariffs, SCADA +12% Foxconn, India +25% ModularConvey Tata/Reliance 60% local ASP +4%, $100M Pune CNC 10% India $10B tools 2026 derisk China 12% CAGR automation.

ROW 3% $74M +12% LATAM mining +16% Chile/Peru HydroClone, Australia LNG, 30% parts/uptime.

Mix services 38% from 34%, China rev 10% from 15% diversification, AI spindles/EquipGuard 15-20% customer gains. Q3 8-10% growth NA/APAC lead, 85% backlog conversion, H2 PMI>50.

Organic revenue growth 8.2% of total 12%/$2.85B +11% CC. Volumes 5.5pts automation/robotics 28% rev +15% DynamoFlex cobots 1.25x btb, material handling +12% Amazon/FedEx, aero +6% Boeing/Airbus. Pricing 2.7pts 4-6% increases 90% realization IoT CNC premium 15-20% vs Haas.

NA 10.4% IIJA earthmoving conveyors $4.2B backlog +18%, EMEA 7.1% electrification welding Vestas-like, APAC 5.8% China semis TSMC Japan yen. 'TechStack 2025' $450M digital twins sustainable fluids +150bps share vs Fanuc/ABB 12wk leads.

Inorganic 3.8pts $105M: Precision RoboTech $620M Feb semi arms 2.4pts $68M +22% cross-sell Intel/Samsung >15% IRR; EuroForge $280M Aug presses 1.4pts $37M EV powertrain. $22M synergies 75% ahead procurement -12% steel G&A, >10% EBITDA adjacent accretive yr1, margins +150bps 18.2%.

Q4 organic 7-9% total mid-teens $12.5B backlog reshoring labor green H2.

Macro factors on end markets: ISM PMI 49.2 up Q2 47.8 contraction but inflation 3.2% from 6.8% stabilizing steel/copper/semis, rates Fed 5.25-5.50 ECB 4 PBOC steady crimp capex. Book-to-bill 1.15x bifurcated secular vs cyclical.

Semis 15% +14% CHIPS TSMC AZ Intel OH Samsung TX cleanroom robots litho, consumer elec -4% IDC destock end fab 82%. 'MachSmart' Siemens MindSphere -25% downtime Deere $150M annuities pricing 4.2%>2.8% infl EBITDA 22.1% turns 4.2x Nucor partners battery 15% 2025 $220M Euro robotics 10% cobots. Q4 stabilize Fed 75bps cuts aero/semis mid-singles $12.5B backlog 45% gross 25% ROIC >Ingersoll/nVent.

Automation/digital $285M +32% YoY +8% seq outpace mech 1500bps. Hardware 25% $165M cobots AGVs, digital SaaS analytics edge 45% $120M 42% mix from 32% ARR $420M +38% NRR 118%. IIoT 16% CAGR McKinsey labor vac +22% BLS install 12k sites 99.4% uptime AI PM.

IntelliForge NVIDIA Jetson digital twin 95% acc virtual comm -40% v3.0 genAI anomaly spindle/hyd MTTR min Rockwell FactoryTalk $50M EV bat. Customer OEE +18% 92% downtime -27% energy -15% ROI 3.2x 18mo throughput 12-22% AutoLink retro services 72% +450bps seg 51% +320bps.

APAC 42% China2025 India PLI cobots +35% digital 48%, EMEA 28% Green Deal VFD IPCEI 20% grants, Americas 22% triple PMI CHIPS $120M fab. Capex R&D +15% $180M 5G vision quantum cyber JV Fanuc palletizers Q4 30%+ FY25 28% rev 50%+ margins.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value.

Now, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, David. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our manufacturing processes, improving supply chain efficiency, and enhancing our customer service capabilities across construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing. Demand in construction up 15% NA IIJA IRA hybrid excavators X-Force data centers +18% loaders, EMEA +7% rail renewables India +12% China -8% LatAm +10%, Site Optimization telematics +22% parts Q4 mid-singles infra floor. Mining +14% EV copper/gold trucks Command BEV loaders +25% battery metals Aus/Indo +22% NA flat APAC exp EMEA copper $200M frames capex $150B Wood Mac aftermarket +18%. Ag +4% precision tractors AutoPath +12% combines NA corn Brazil -3% EMEA flat APAC rice +9% Farm Command yields +15% CNH share Q4 low-single buffer 30% aftermarket. Manufacturing +11% reshoring CNC AGVs Fanuc semis EV CHIPS +16% IPCEI +9% China2025 Smart Factory -25% downtime Tesla $50B US capex Deloitte. We're leveraging digital technologies and data analytics to drive operational excellence, with enterprise 6-9% organic mining/const offset ag, margins +220bps 28.5% pricing tech R&D $1.2B electrify 20% green $300B McKinsey. We're also focused on ensuring the health and safety of our employees.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, and the Internet of Things. We are developing solutions to improve predictive maintenance, optimize customer operations, and enhance product performance. Our new IntelliForge platform is significantly impacting the market, with install base expansion, high uptime, efficiency gains like OEE improvements and energy savings, and strong growth in digital recurring revenue pulling segment margins higher.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long term impact of the new IntelliForge platform on your revenue and profitability?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Alex. The IntelliForge platform is poised for substantial long-term revenue and profitability uplift as it transforms us into a systems integrator. With ARR already at $420 million growing 38% and NRR at 118%, digital services are shifting our mix to 42% high-margin SaaS, targeting 28% of total revenue by FY25 at over 50% margins. Customer ROI of 3.2x drives repeat business and expansions, while hardware like cobots and AGVs benefit from ecosystem lock-in. We've seen services margins expand 450 bps to 72%, and overall, it's compounding share gains in IIoT, with capex in 5G and AI ensuring leadership. Expect it to contribute 5-7% to annual growth, with profitability accretion of 200-300 bps annually as adoption hits 50% of installs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (Goldman Sachs):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

David Chen:
Good question, Maria. For FY25, we're guiding total revenue growth to 10-13%, with organic at 8-10% driven by backlog conversion, pricing, and automation/digital momentum. Inorganic could add 2-3% from pipeline tuck-ins. NA and APAC lead on reshoring and infra, offsetting any EMEA energy lag. Backlog visibility and 1.2x book-to-bill support this, with Q3 at 8-10%. Upside from capex rebound as rates ease, risks balanced by services mix now 38% and liquidity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel (Morgan Stanley):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Michael Reynolds:
Absolutely, Raj. We're accelerating multi-regional diversification to derisk geopolitics, reducing China rev to 10% via India/SE Asia investments like $100M Pune plant targeting 10% machine tool share. NA capex $150M Fort Wayne robotics, EMEA Düsseldorf/warehouses for Green Deal. Mexico Monterrey furnace enhances nearshoring. Overall, friendshoring to Vietnam/India, localized content 60-80%, positions us for 12% APAC CAGR and sustained NA strength on CHIPS/IIJA.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Kim (Barclays):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

Lisa Patel:
Chris, energy costs are up but manageable via efficiency and hedging. Digital twins optimize consumption -15% per unit, hybrid/BEV fleets cut diesel, JIT/VMI reduces holding costs. Multi-sourcing Mexico/Vietnam avoids EU spikes, forward contracts $200M cover 70%. Operational levers like AI toolpathing + spindle efficiency yield 18% OEE gains, protecting 42% gross. Green initiatives qualify for EU grants, renewables exposure offsets oil vol.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the Q&A.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Titan Equipment Inc. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
